title: Capacity-blocked chip-firing: sharp weighted bound and a live-set characterization
statement: Let a finite loopless directed multigraph have an absorbing sink, nonsink arcs strictly forward in a fixed vertex order, and every nonsink vertex reaching the sink. Let b(v) bound incoming multiplicity, m(u,v) <= b(v) for all u, and assume d(v) + b(v) <= C(v) + 1, equivalently C(v) >= d(v) + max_u m(u,v) - 1 when b is the maximum. Then capacity-blocked firing terminates and every reachable capacity-terminal state is the ordinary normal form of its initial state. The unit-edge hypothesis C(v) >= d(v) is the case b = 1. Conversely, if the arc relation contains a directed cycle then preservation fails at every capacity with C(v) >= d(v); the two cases partition the model. Over arbitrary digraphs and arbitrary capacities, writing Live v for outdegree v <= capacity v, transfer holds exactly when the live subgraph is rank-ordered, satisfies outdegree v + mult u v <= capacity v + 1 on live arcs, and is closed under arcs out of live vertices.
resolves: CBMD-DYN-CAPACITY-FIRING-001 open successor: the named candidate C(v) >= d(v) + max_u m(u,v) - 1
verified: The weighted overflow lemma, preservation of terminal states, and the full weighted transfer theorem compile under Lean 4.35.0 with no sorry, admit, or axiom declaration in the source.

Observed axiom dependencies from actual #print axioms output are exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; weighted_overflow_forces_unstable depends only on propext and unit_case_capacity_admits on none.
Exact enumeration found no failure at the bound across 8364 systems at n<=3 with multiplicity <=3, and 4596 systems at n<=4 with multiplicity <=2.
A separately implemented checker verified the theorem's own conclusion, that every capacity-terminal state equals the ordinary normal form, over 96053 initial states with zero disagreements.

Sharpness: lowering the bound by one at a single receiver of incoming multiplicity at least two produced 1344 transfer failures at n<=3 and 7544 at n<=4, and 17682 terminal disagreements in the independent adverse control.
A positive control reproduces failure at C(v) = d(v): 936 systems at n<=3 and 4256 at n<=4.
The checks gate on the transfer property rather than on nonconfluence, after enumeration showed the smallest C=d failure is confluent with a single wrong normal form.

The cycle obstruction compiles: a directed cycle plus C(v) >= d(v) yields a capacity-terminal state that is not ordinarily stable, built from the capacities themselves and therefore surviving every enlargement.
A forward ordering provably excludes the cycle structure used by that obstruction (ordered_has_no_closed_set, axiom dependency propext alone).
The cycle obstruction witness is confirmed in all 27,440 tested cyclic graph and capacity pairs, and an exhaustive state sweep found no cyclic system preserving transfer at any slack from 0 to 4.

Sufficiency over arbitrary digraphs compiles: under the three live-set conditions an admissible capacity-terminal state is ordinarily stable; vertices outside the live set are permanently ordinarily stable and need no argument.
A single filled-set obstruction compiles and yields both the cycle failure and the live-to-dead failure as instances; liveToDeadFilledSet constructs the two-member case and depends on no axioms.

Exactness census: over 798,025 systems (n<=3, multiplicity<=2, unit sink arcs, every capacity in 0..d(v)+2) the three conditions agree with the exact transfer property in every case, with zero unsound and zero incomplete.

Minimality: dropping ordered-on-live makes the predicate wrong on 63,847 systems, dropping the bound on 4,998, and dropping live-closed on 393,192; no drop produces an incomplete predicate, so the conditions are independent.

Necessity of the bound is proved: violating it on a live arc yields an explicit capacity-terminal state that is not ordinarily stable, with the truncated-subtraction branch handled rather than assumed away.
Necessity of live-closure is proved via the two-member filled set, which depends on no axioms.
Ordering together with live-closure provably admit no filled-set obstruction at all (depends on propext alone), so the sufficient conditions are exactly strong enough to exclude the obstruction.
unresolved: novelty assessment and external specialist review
necessity of the bound at receivers of incoming multiplicity one

the step from 'no rank function on the live subgraph' to a concrete directed cycle: the classical finite-digraph topological-order fact, not proved here and the sole gap between the compiled theorems and the census
nonclaims: not a novelty determination; the capacity rule is classical finite-capacity Petri-net semantics and the ordinary chip-firing theory is classical and assumed
not an external independent verification; the second implementation is separately written but not externally authored
finite enumeration corroborates the theorem and does not prove it
ordinary well-foundedness and uniqueness enter as explicit hypotheses and are not proved here
the cycle obstruction assumes every vertex has positive outdegree and says nothing about capacities below d(v)
the characterization's exactness is a finite census result, not a proved equivalence
smallest_decisive_test: Exhibit an ordered multigraph satisfying d(v) + max_u m(u,v) <= C(v) + 1 with a reachable capacity-terminal state that is not the ordinary normal form of its initial state; or a reference proving the same preservation statement with an explicit semantic translation.
